revision_note: r3 (2026-09-17): the wall is modelled as it is built (mechanical/fixed_heat_common.py): a 2 mm inner web, a 2 mm gap layer that contains only discrete bridge blocks, and an 8 mm external radiator panel, all one solid. The lugs bolt to the inner web; the panel is reached through the 2 mm web laterally to the nearest bridge. thermal_cf1.py therefore carries the two webs as their own 2 mm in-plane sheets coupled to the panels at the bridge patches read from results/mechanical/WEB_FACE_PROBE_CF1.json; the r2 'skin/stiffener/half-plate' series term was a misreading of 1 mm slab data and is withdrawn. The carrier node is defined at the arch shelf / +Y-riser junction and the arch riser conduction is booked on both links.
role: Single source of truth for the CF1 conduction path: read by thermal_path_cf1.step.py (solids), thermal_cf1.py (link resistances; web sheets and bridges come from the probe receipt), verify_thermal_cf1.py (independent recomputation) and probe_web_faces_cf1.py (lug footprints).

frame.part_frame: module mm, identical to coupled_closure/mechanical_parts.py (board XY with KiCad y negated, board top face z=0)
frame.module_bbox_note: V30 lug module compound (56 instances) at this pose, from results/mechanical/MODULE_POSE_NARROWPHASE_CF1.json; 194 mm wide with 4.4 mm of hardware below the plate. The design-spec 'cavity' statement referred to the carrier box only and is superseded by the exact module-pose test.
frame.carrier_node_definition: lumped node at the arch shelf / +Y riser junction (module z 27..32). Q201 case -> node (IF_CF1_01 budget 1.5 K/W) = TIM 0.54 + riser B climb 0.47 + shelf span 0.32 = 1.33 K/W. Boss heat (copper, shunts, fuse, ~5 W) physically enters the plate, not the arch; it is lumped at the node (disclosed simplification).

material.note: 6061-T6 handbook conductivity for boss/straps/lugs; 130 W/mK is the wall conductivity used by tools/spatial_radiator_network.py Sheet(k=130) and is applied to the 2 mm web sheets and the bridges. No certificate, no lot traceability.

TIM.note: Same TIM family and 25 psi clamp point as thermal/SPATIAL_RADIATOR_NETWORK_SCREEN.json. Clamp force that realises 25 psi is NOT yet designed.

web_model.description: Each wall's 2 mm inner web is a non-radiating Sheet (same 344x180 face frame and holes as its panel, thickness scaled from the Sheet default 8 mm). The lug patch sits on the web sheet. Each gap-layer bridge block couples the web sheet to the panel sheet with R = gap_thickness / (k_web * bridge_area). The parent CHB cold-finger links keep their endpoints on the panels.
web_model.requirement: gap_material_under_lug_mm3 must be 0 for both lugs (no bridge under the lug), otherwise a through term would also be needed

carrier_path.name: arch_riser_A_descent
carrier_path.basis: node at the shelf mid-plane (module z 29.5) down the +Y riser (module y 1..6) to the plate top (module z -7.6)

carrier_path.name: plate_spreading_1D
carrier_path.basis: 1-D full carrier width from the riser foot (S y ~31) to the strap contact centroid (S y -36) through the 4 mm plate; crude, a 2-D solution for the 25 mm-wide contact would be lower

minus_Y.conduction_length_basis: centroid of the 25x40 carrier contact (S y -36) to the lug TIM face (S y -93.15)
minus_Y.sink_face: CF1_LUG_MINUS_Y inner face, S y -93.15; lug outer face on the 2 mm web at S y -101.15

carrier_path.name: arch_riser_A_to_paddle_centroid
carrier_path.basis: node at the shelf mid-plane (module z 29.5) down the +Y riser to the arch-paddle centroid (module z 16.4); the paddle spans z 1.4..31.4 so heat enters along the riser height

plus_Y.conduction_length_basis: arch face (S y 36) to the lug TIM face (S y 93.15)
plus_Y.sink_face: CF1_LUG_PLUS_Y inner face, S y 93.15; lug outer face on the 2 mm web at S y 101.15

link_model: R_link = sum(carrier_path L/(k A)) + R_TIM(source) + L_cond/(k A_cond) + R_TIM(sink) + lug_through/(k A_sink); the link ends on the 2 mm web sheet at the lug patch. Web lateral conduction and the bridge coupling to the radiating panel are solved by the sheet model, not by a scalar term.
excluded_from_the_1D_link_model: 2-D spreading in the carrier plate (1-D full-width term used instead), in the lugs and at the strap-to-web contact
fastener and joint conduction in parallel with the TIM
contact pressure non-uniformity across the pads
radiation exchange between the strap and its surroundings and from the inner webs to the interior (webs are treated as adiabatic on their inner side)
thermal expansion, preload relaxation and vibration
the arch riser B and shelf conduction between Q201 and the node (inside the IF_CF1_01 1.5 K/W budget)

source_discrepancies.finding: Same STEP (sha256 eafde8dd...) at two poses: MAIN_INPUT_PLACEMENT_BOUNDS_V27.json translation (-115, 39, 14) rotated (bbox S x -152.5..-77.5) versus thermal/RADIATOR_OBSTACLE_BOUNDS.json translation (10, -48, 14) unrotated (bbox S x -35..55, top S z 34). The -Y strap sits above S z 35, clear of both.

MAIN_INPUT_PLACEMENT_BOUNDS_V27.json binds shear_web_1 to mechanical/wall_navigation_bosses.step while thermal/RADIATOR_OBSTACLE_BOUNDS.json binds it to mechanical/fixed_heat_wall_pos.step (different sha256). The probe reads the V27 binding; the two files give the same slab profile inside the +Y lug footprint. See results/mechanical/WEB_FACE_PROBE_CF1.json webs.shear_web_1.thermal_side_binding.
source_discrepancies.disposition: OPEN_UPSTREAM; no geometric consequence for the lug
